subject: DONE s321: suite runner joined TAP by NUMBER — manufactured false failures after any count divergence
description:
FIXED s321. tools/run-perl-suite.pl's per-test failure log joined perl's and PCL's TAP streams on the test NUMBER. Any file where PCL emits extra or missing rows mid-file then has EVERY subsequent row mis-attributed — in both directions: rows that pass get reported as failures, and rows that fail get silently credited.

Worked example (op/do.t): the file asserts `do subname()` is a syntax error and guards each assertion with a fail() that fires if the sub is called. PCL DOES call it (the blessed principle-9 divergence), so PCL emits 2 extra rows and runs +2 ahead from there. The log accused t67 ("result of delete(helem) is copied") and t70 ("$@ is false on do dir") — BOTH PASS, probed in isolation and confirmed in the raw PCL TAP.

Fix: tools/lib/PclTapAlign.pm (tap_rows + align_taps) pairs the streams BY DESCRIPTION, re-syncing only on positive evidence — an exact description match found ahead within a 20-row window, CONFIRMED by a second match for the following perl row. Empty descriptions and value-interpolated descriptions (which legitimately differ exactly when a test fails) find no match and fall through to positional pairing, i.e. the old behaviour. Unit tests: tools/t/tap-align.t (14 rows, incl. 4 inverse guards: interpolated descs, unnamed rows, repeated descs, out-of-window matches). The faillog now shows PCL's own number when it differs, names each PCL-only row individually, and prints a "renumbered" marker row.

Consequence for the R1 gate: this had to land BEFORE the S2 snapshot, because the FIXTURE registry (#172) matches per-ROW against this log. Also note the old tap_map is deleted; its `[ \t]` gotcha (s316o, 421 phantom rows on op/signatures.t) is carried into the module.

FOLLOW-UP CHECKED s321 — the SWEEP does NOT have this bug: tools/sweep-diff.pl keys every row on "$file\t$desc" (description), not on the test number, so the 690-row baseline is not affected.

STILL OPEN (do during S2, no Fable input needed): existing perl-suite-expected.tsv rows whose REASON makes a per-row claim ("t19 is the ONLY failing row…") were reasoned from the old number-joined log. The new log prints a "renumbered" marker, so cross-check any file that emits one against its registration.
